- Reactant (2) contains a **secondary cyclic amine**, which acts as the nucleophile.
- The mesylate group is displaced, while the aryl chloride remains unchanged.
- The N-methylformamide-like component is likely solvent/base-related; sodium salts provide basic conditions.

```text
cyclic amine–N–CH2CH2CH2–n1c(=O)[nH]c2cc(Cl)ccc21
```


Thus, the product is the **tertiary amine formed by replacing –O–SO2CH3 with the nitrogen of the cyclic amine**. The chlorinated heteroaromatic fragment and its C–Cl bond are retained. The retrieved reaction record supports this mesylate-displacement connectivity, although its amine partner is not identical to the encoded second reactant.


The second reactant contains a **secondary cyclic amine**, which undergoes SN2 alkylation at the terminal carbon of the propyl mesylate. The aryl chloride is retained and does not participate.

```text
mesylate–CH2CH2CH2–N(heterocycle)
```
